title: Hiring in September grew much less than expected, jobs report shows
summary:
Hiring in September grew much less than expected, jobs report showsHiring grew much less than expected in September as a monthslong surge of inflation weighed on shoppers and rattled bond markets, according to the federal government's monthly jobs report.
Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, a sharp slowdown from the 162,000 jobs added in August, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed.
Economists expected employers to have added 84,000 jobs last month.
Employment in manufacturing grew at a modest pace, adding 9,000 jobs last month.

title: US unemployment claims dip to 197,000, lowest since mid-July
summary:
The number of people applying for U.S. unemployment benefits dipped last week to the lowest level since mid-July as layoffs remain low and and most American workers enjoy job securityWASHINGTON -- The number of people applying for U.S. unemployment benefits dipped last week to the lowest level since mid-July as layoffs remain low and most American workers enjoy job security.
The Labor Department said Thursday that initial jobless claims ticked down to 197,000 from a revised 198,000 the week before.
The four-week average of claims, which smooths out week-to-week volatility, dropped by 2,500 to 200,000.
Claims for jobless benefits are a proxy for layoffs, and economists watch them because they can be a sign of where the job market is headed.
So far this year, claims have mostly stayed below 220,000 — historically low.
